correctness.rationale: Deleting the maximum contracts just the inserted node: the keys above the prefix maximum constitute its only subtree, and the depth of the inserted node is the prefix record count. This gives (1) for the empty prefix too. On moving the maximum one slot, a new record x adds one to the record count and subtracts x−R from the subtree size, proving (2). For the tail, sample the unordered set of the first t entries, then require its largest element to arrive last (probability 1/t); lowering that largest element by k is a bijection to t-subsets of {1,…,n−1−k} when its spacing from the preceding maximum is at least k+1 (sentinel zero for t=1). This gives (3), and summing gives (4). The relative-order ranks of the prefix are independent uniform ranks, independent of the set of prefix values; this gives the two factors in (5). The standard root split gives the base mean in (6). At t=n−1 there can be no positive jump; at n=2 the only gap is zero. The conditional law is under uniform insertions, not uniform tree shapes. The suggested subtraction direction in the middle of proof §Exact decrement tails (RESULT.md line 56) is reversed; (4), (6), the final subtraction and the independent tail-sum proof give the correct sign. Own replay via recursive root splitting, exhaustive base permutations for 2≤n≤8, verifies (1)–(6), with tails computed from actual path-length differences and the PGF checked as exact coefficient counts. This finite check supplements the all-n argument.
residual_risks: Only ordinary unbalanced BSTs under the stated distinct-key convention; (5) is for the increment and does not factor the full path-length law.

broader_coverage.reasoning: General unconditioned PGFs and moments do not specify the neighboring-gap law of the common-permutation coupling; one must identify and count the events after changing the arrival time.

evidence: The same-day covariance equals 3n+H_n−2(n+1)H_n^(2), with an accompanying response to a full-spine tilt. It is not a joint or conditional statement for the position of n.

Prodinger indexes pairs by key and takes minima of insertion times on key intervals. This is an exact alternative encoding of total path length, not a different BST model.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Comparing the encodings exposes overlap in the tools: deleting the last key index n in Prodinger's formula leaves only pairs ending at n, and sorting those pairs into the two endpoint-minimum events recovers (1). Extracting and evaluating the coupled changes across all slots and their finite-sample laws is not an identity stated for that encoding in the inspected source.

value.rationale: A natural arrival statistic for the extreme key affects a canonical global search-cost statistic. The result orders every conditional law in one coupling and measures exactly when and by how much neighboring slots differ, including the terminal equality; this is more informative than another moment of the unconditioned path length.
